name: Chronograph watch

image.caption: Detailed view of dial of chronograph watch

lead: A chronograph is a watch that combines a stopwatch with ordinary timekeeping. It typically shows a central seconds hand for timing, small subdials for elapsed minutes or hours, and two pushers beside the crown for starting, stopping and resetting.

For appearance, the busy dial with subdials and often a tachymeter scale is a recognisable sports or aviation look, and watches are a staple of men's style. Forum members also use them in practice for timing sprints, rest periods and hikes.

paras: People wear it as a daily watch and use the pushers to time events. Forum users mention timing interval training and hiking with a chronograph, and discuss choosing between cheap sport models and higher-end mechanical ones.
There is little risk beyond cost and the usual care for water resistance. A chronograph describes the stopwatch function; a separate 'chronometer' label is a certification of accuracy.

chain: Wear a chronograph on the wrist
Dial adds a technical, sporty detail
Completes an outfit and doubles as a timer
angle.text: The watch adds a visible accessory to the wrist, with subdials and often a tachymeter bezel giving a sporty look. It also lets the wearer time workouts or activities.

lead: A chronograph is a watch that combines a stopwatch with a standard timepiece. The stopwatch can be started, stopped and reset by the user, and the face usually has a central seconds hand plus subdials tracking elapsed minutes and sometimes hours.[1]
Start/stop is normally a pusher at about the 2 o'clock position and reset at about 4 o'clock. Many models add a tachymeter scale on the bezel for calculating speed over a timed distance.[1]

As a style item, the layered dial makes it a recognisable sports-watch look. Lifters and athletes on forums also describe using one for sprints, rest timing and hiking, so it serves both as an accessory and a tool.[2][3]

paras: Internal wheels turning at one-second, one-minute and one-hour rates record elapsed time, with more complex models adding subdials for fractions of a second, moon phase or 24-hour time.[1] Variants include flyback, rattrapante (double chronograph), automatic, digital and specialised diver types.[1]
A chronograph is a function, whereas a chronometer is a performance certification from Switzerland's COSC; a watch can be both.[1]
Louis Moinet is credited with an early astronomical chronograph in 1816, and Nicolas Mathieu Rieussec made the first marketed one in 1821 to time horse races. Adolphe Nicole added reset in 1844.[1]

Longines produced an early wristwatch chronograph movement in 1913, and the Breitlings added the central seconds hand and the two-pusher layout between 1915 and 1934. Heuer introduced a rotating tachymeter bezel in 1958, and automatic chronographs reached market in 1969.[1] Omega Speedmasters were worn by NASA astronauts on Apollo missions.[1]

sections.h: Use in looksmaxxing and fitness culture
paras: On T Nation, one member described using a Timex Expedition as an alarm clock, timer for sprints and rest periods and a chronograph for hiking, saying they 'feel naked' without it.[3] Another thread asks which watch suits interval training, with Timex Ironman models recommended by other members.[4] Style-focused threads discuss which watches are acceptable as everyday wear.[2]
